local_build_workspace.toolchain_status: RESOLVED 2026-10-08. The x86-64 toolchain runs natively under Rosetta 2 inside an amd64 Apple-container VM (`container run -d --name smk-build --arch amd64 ubuntu:24.04`): uname -m reports x86_64 and every toolchain binary executes unmodified. The qemu-user + LD_PRELOAD shim of docs/from-scratch-platform-plan.md section 7 is superseded and is not needed. One non-obvious dependency: the linker driver /opt/jieli/pi32v2/bin/lto-wrapper is a '#!/usr/bin/env python3' script, so the base image needs python3 (without it the link stops at "/usr/bin/env: 'python3': No such file or directory", make Error 127, after all 17 sources compiled cleanly). Exact reproduction commands: docs/linux-build-flash-procedure.md section 3. Working build: known_builds[1].

allowed.name: RAM0 below the stock v15 high-water mark
allowed.reason: On-chip SRAM span the stock v15 image provably initializes/uses (initialized-data copy destination through the BSS/heap zero span). Boot stack sits inside it (sp=0x01c3a2d4).

allowed.name: wl82 cache RAM window (envelope)
allowed.reason: Envelope of the SDK cache_ram region: ORIGIN = 0x1f20000 + (8-FREE_IACHE_WAY)*4K, LENGTH = (FREE_DACHE_WAY + FREE_IACHE_WAY)*4K, so the exact extent depends on the freed cache ways of a given build

allowed.name: SDK BOOT_INFO slot (48 B)
allowed.reason: Shared platform convention, live in stock firmware: boot code 0x020000C6 copies six fields into this 48-byte slot. SDK linker emits .boot_info here.

allowed.name: SDK UPDATA_BEG update-flag region (128 B)
allowed.reason: Shared platform convention, read by the stock boot chain (FUN_02007424).

forbidden.name: SDRAM window declared by the SDK default ('sdram') layout
forbidden.reason: SDRAM presence and controller bring-up on this unit are UNPROVEN, the part-number memory code excludes SDRAM/PSRAM members, and the stock v15 app never addresses it. The 2026-08-15 flashed SDK app placed .data/.bss/heap here and the unit never re-enumerated. This is the P4 gate's reason for refusing a build.

unproven.name: RAM0 above the stock v15 high-water mark
unproven.reason: No evidence of ownership or absence of alias. M09 was lost to exactly this reasoning error ('undecoded and zero' treated as available). An SDK app must not place .data/.bss/heap here until ownership is proven.

known_builds.what: FIRST ARTIFACT THAT ORIGINATES FROM THE PROJECT'S OWN SOURCE. Same no-SDRAM demo_hello base and same app Makefile as known_builds[1], but the device-side SMK OTA transport/packet layer ac79/app/smk_ota_transport.c is compiled into the app, linked into the image, and called once from app_main(), which stores the result in a static volatile and prints PASS/FAIL on the normal demo console. The layer is the packet/transport half of the device-side mirror that docs/self-recovering-sdk-app.md section 6 designates src/protocol.c for: it encodes the 15-byte device->host request packets and decodes the host->device update/ACK packets exactly as src/protocol.c does on the host, using the same checksum and 7-bit framing. It carries NO USB descriptor or enumeration work (stage B1), NO MIDI endpoint I/O (stage B2), NO session or flash policy (stage B3); it never reads or writes flash and never touches USB. OFFLINE ARTIFACT ONLY: never flashed, never packed into a package, no device contact of any kind, and its run-time behaviour on hardware is UNVERIFIED (the boot-time self-test result has not been observed on a device).

known_builds.what: STAGE B1: the app now carries the updater USB personality 4d4a:4155. Built on known_builds[2] (same base, Makefile and call site) and adding ac79/app/smk_usb_descriptors.c: the 18-byte device descriptor recovered byte for byte from flash 0x0BDDE5 of the live dumps, an AUTHORED 39-byte config set (one MIDIStreaming interface, bulk OUT 0x04 / IN 0x84, bus powered, 100 mA), a GET_DESCRIPTOR-style table lookup, and a boot self-test called from app_main() next to the transport self-test. GROUND TRUTH vs AUTHORED is kept strictly apart in the source: the device descriptor is evidence, the config/interface/endpoint bytes are authored because no artifact contains them, and the parts the plan does not specify (MIDI jack descriptors, CS_ENDPOINT descriptors, string descriptors) are omitted rather than invented - the string indices the recovered descriptor names (iManufacturer=1, iProduct=2) are reported absent, not filled with made-up text. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not initialise any USB controller, does not hand any descriptor to a USB engine, does not enumerate, and does no endpoint or transfer work - so the identity is what the app WOULD present, verified at source level against the flash dump, not an observed enumeration. No flash access, no boot-sector involvement, never flashed or packed, no device contact of any kind, and no run-time behaviour on hardware has been observed.

usb_descriptor_evidence.recon: ac79/evidence/recon_updater_usb_identity.py -> ac79/evidence/updater-usb-identity.json. Searched 18 whole-flash 1 MiB dumps, 47 app-slot payloads, 607 other captures and the project's own SDK builds. The updater identity 4d4a:4155 occurs in 16 of the 18 whole-flash dumps, always at flash 0x0BDDED, always with the identical 18-byte device descriptor at 0x0BDDE5; 0 occurrences in all 47 app-slot payloads, which is why a replacement app cannot inherit it. The two dumps without it are the pre-restore 2026-07-14 image and its copy, used as the negative control.
usb_descriptor_evidence.site_structure: In the dumps the descriptor is not part of a USB descriptor table: it sits inside a short package record introduced by an ASCII marker (2f 2a 2e 75 66 77 = a slash, a star, ".ufw"), 17 bytes before the descriptor, then the 10-byte trailer 01 04 F0 22 24 07 35 7D F7 00, then 0xFF fill to the 4 KiB sector boundary 0x0BE000. Nothing descriptor-shaped adjoins it.
usb_descriptor_evidence.not_recoverable: 0 config descriptor chains (bLength 9, type 2, chaining to an interface descriptor and summing to its wTotalLength), 0 MIDIStreaming CS_INTERFACE headers (07 24 06), and 0 endpoint descriptors for 0x04 or 0x84 (07 05 04 ... / 07 05 84 ...) across every corpus searched. So of the descriptor set the plan needs, only the 18-byte device descriptor is recoverable; the config, interface, endpoint and string descriptors are authored, and this is stated as authored in the source and in the test output rather than presented as ground truth.
usb_descriptor_evidence.host_check: ac79/test/usb_descriptor_test.c (make test-usb-descriptors) checks the descriptor set the app would present against real dumps: 12 checks / 0 failures without a dump, 22 checks / 0 failures with one, and a sweep of 18 files gave 175 checks / 0 failures with 15 whole-flash dumps verified byte for byte against flash 0x0BDDE5 plus 1 negative control. It re-runs the absence searches on every invocation, so the authored bytes stay falsifiable: if a future dump contains a config/interface/endpoint set, the test fails and demands the authored bytes be replaced by the recovered ones.

open_questions.question: The SDK links at 0x02000120 (ENTRY) while the stock v15 runtime window is recorded as 0x02000000 + file offset. The 0x120 offset's meaning for an app-only OTA package is not resolved.
open_questions.resolution: No conflict existed: the two conventions are one mapping seen from two anchors, and 0x120 is declared by the image itself. The app.bin JLFS entry header sits at flash 0x4020 and declares offset = 0x120 (the module's own assertion is require(app.offset == 0x120 and app.size == APP_DATA_SIZE)), while APP_DATA_OFFSET = 0x4120 is declared in that module as a plain literal, not as a base-plus-offset expression; this map DERIVES 0x4120 == 0x4000 + 0x120 by checked arithmetic rather than quoting a declared 'base + 0x120', and that derivation is what places the offset relative to the app-area base 0x4000. Therefore flash 0x4000 (app_area_head, which is also app-image file offset 0) maps to VA 0x02000000, and the payload's first byte at flash 0x4120 maps to VA 0x02000120 = the SDK .text VMA = ENTRY = isd_config.ini ENTRY. v2-rx-001's 'file offset + 0x02000000' is the app-image-relative convention, not flash-absolute (0x02000000 + 0x4120 = 0x02004120 would be wrong). Arithmetic proof that the window is exactly the payload slot: v2-rx-001 end 0x02096A34 - ENTRY 0x02000120 = 0x96914 = 616,724 = 617,012 - 0x120, i.e. the window spans precisely APP_DATA_SIZE bytes from the declared offset onward. The new build lands .text at 0x02000120..0x02014FE0, inside the window with 531,028 B of headroom.

open_questions.question: The flash app area is 615,731 B (0x4300..0x9A833) while the v15 app.bin ceiling used by the gate is 617,012 B. The 1,281 B difference must be resolved before any replacement app is flashed; neither number may be silently substituted for the other.
open_questions.resolution: Both numbers are correct and measure different spans of the same application; the 1,281 B decomposes exactly into 480 B + 801 B, one term per boundary. 617,012 B is the app-data payload slot: the app.bin entry header declares offset=0x120 and size=0x96A34, so the payload occupies flash 0x4120..0x9AB54, and this is the number the packer pads to with 0xFF, i.e. the only valid ceiling for a replacement app.bin (pack_sdk_app_fwsc.py: require(len(app_bin) <= APP_DATA_SIZE)). 615,731 B is the v15-image-specific region an app-only OTA/restore may replace, 0x4300..0x9A833 (v2-fl-004): it starts 480 B later because it excludes the whole JLFS header sector 0x4000..0x4300 (which carries app_area_head at 0x4000, the app.bin entry header at 0x4020, and the first 480 B of payload), and it ends 801 B earlier because v15's occupied app extent ends at 0x9A833 while the payload slot runs on to 0x9AB54. The near-miss 0x9AD33 - 0x9A833 = 0x500 = 1,280 that made an off-by-one explanation look plausible is unrelated: it is the version-dependent tail (v2-fl-005), not the ceiling. The declared area itself is 0x4000..0x9ACD3 = 617,683 B = 288 B headers (32 B area + 256 B entry) + 617,012 B payload + 383 B trailer. Practical rule: size a replacement app.bin against 617,012 B and never against 615,731 B; and never write 617,012 B starting at 0x4300 (that would overrun v15's app end into tail metadata).
